recognize_zh: CSF 抹片中一小群細胞核偏心、染色質呈粗塊狀、細胞質深藍且可見核旁淡染區（hof），外觀為漿細胞群，在骨髓瘤病人即為 CSF 漿細胞增多（中樞侵犯）。
features: Small aggregate of seven mononuclear cells on a clean cytospin background
Eccentric round to oval nuclei with coarse, clumped chromatin
Deeply basophilic cytoplasm with a paler perinuclear zone (hof) in several cells
Cells are relatively uniform, medium-sized, with irregular cytoplasmic contours and small blebs
Nucleoli not conspicuous; no admixed lymphocytes, neutrophils or red cells
describe_en: Cytospin of cerebrospinal fluid shows a small cluster of uniform plasma cells with eccentric nuclei, coarsely clumped chromatin and deeply basophilic cytoplasm, several showing a perinuclear hof. The cells lack admixed reactive lymphocytes or monocytes. The clustering reflects cytocentrifuge aggregation rather than true epithelial cohesion. In a patient with known multiple myeloma and neurologic symptoms, findings are consistent with CSF plasmacytosis due to CNS involvement by plasma cell myeloma, which can be confirmed by flow cytometry for clonal plasma cells.

ddx.vs: Reactive plasma cells are few and mixed with lymphocytes and monocytes, and flow cytometry shows polytypic light chains.
Carcinoma cells form truly cohesive three-dimensional clusters with nuclear molding, macronucleoli and cytokeratin positivity.
Contains a spectrum of small lymphocytes and plasmacytoid cells with CD19/CD20 expression, rather than pure CD138+/CD19- plasma cells.
